sharedRules.connectionOrder: Storage is always first in both the Connections dialog and the control-panel icon order, followed by AI, GPU and publishing connections; independent of connection state.

Not exposed: replaced by theme preset radio selection

theme.persistence: Selected preset ID in localStorage (ecco-theme-preset-v1); prior custom palette is no longer used
theme.default: Original declaration colors retained as CSS variable fallbacks
theme.scope: Existing presets are color-only. Ocean and Dark Sky add translucent surfaces, backdrop blur, blue borders and background gradients without changing layout, typography, controls or media.
theme.runtime: theme.js bridges accessible CSS declarations and dynamic inline styles to shared color variables; media pixels are unchanged
theme.selection: Single preset, saved immediately; pointer exit retracts the panel; no popup or color inputs Default is always the first item.
theme.connectionStatusScope: GPU connection buttons and the AI, Storage, GPU and Publishing connection control panel icons share the same connected/disconnected colors. Desert uses dark brown #3c2c20 when connected and light brown #8c6844 when disconnected.

glass.approval: User approved Ocean (light clear glass) and Dark Sky (dark blue glass), with ocean-blue accents replacing yellow.
glass.surfaces: Header, navigation, panels, cards, menus, dialogs and controls; backdrop blur only, never media blur.
glass.backdrop: Light coastal gradient for Ocean; midnight blue gradient for Dark Sky. No mockup UI or sample media embedded.
glass.fallback: Opaque surfaces when backdrop-filter is unsupported or reduced transparency is preferred.
glass.persistence: Existing theme preference; switching away removes glass styling.

activityPanel.title: Activity, Logs and Errors
activityPanel.connectivity: Activity contains expandable credential-redacted connection checks, attempts, outcomes and issues, latest 500 retained per browser. Failures also appear in Errors with timestamp, user/session, instance, stage and detail.

acceleratorConnections.layout: Two existing GPU cards, one for B200 and one for A100
acceleratorConnections.selection: Each card contains a RunPod instance dropdown; no instance selected by default
acceleratorConnections.status: Fresh relay health controls availability. Distinguish No heartbeat, Heartbeat lost, Service not ready and Available; do not infer RunPod power state. Visible existing help-text paragraph explains failed check.
acceleratorConnections.connection: Explicit Connect adds that instance without removing any existing connection, including another instance in the same class
acceleratorConnections.persistence: Connected instance IDs persist in this browser and require fresh authenticated health before displaying Connected
acceleratorConnections.styling: Existing gpu-grid, gpu-card, dropdown and secondary button rules; no new dimensions
acceleratorConnections.connectedText: Uses the theme connected color: yellow in Default and Forest, mint in Dark Mode, dark brown in Desert. Connected buttons retain full opacity when disabled.

buttonColors.themes: Uses the existing connected/disconnected theme colors, with the unavailable text at 55% opacity

generationCompute.label: Compute
generationCompute.imageAndVideo: Connected GPU instances only; selection drives per-instance model readiness and request routing
generationCompute.audio: Only audio compute classes with a fresh ready worker: CPU, A100 or B200. Existing backend routes by compute class.
generationCompute.empty: Disabled placeholder when no eligible compute is connected
generationCompute.disconnection: Clear displayed selection; never silently switch compute
generationCompute.appearance: Existing generation-section and native select styles; no new dimensions

errorKnowledge.matching: Structured error code first, then known message patterns
errorKnowledge.popup: Friendly message plus Possible cause for recognized issues; existing popup size, theme and local close behavior
errorKnowledge.unknown: Original message retained; no invented diagnosis
errorKnowledge.diagnostics: Original Error stack and model/compute context retained in Errors

clipProgress.layout: One compact 6px bar per clip, maximum group width 440px; clip number and status on same row
clipProgress.fill: Current theme accent; Default yellow; completed clips 100%, waiting clips empty
clipProgress.details: Plain English total clips, current clip, and active clip segment and step counts
clipProgress.percent: Approximate generation progress from segment and step counts, capped at 99 until clip completes; not a time estimate
clipProgress.placement: Main Video tab directly under Review videos, before generated outputs; Pause after next clip and Stop after next clip below bars. Activity has text status only.

storyJourneys.approval: 2026-10-20: compact story buttons with dropdown arrows and right-side category submenus; tailored second screens
storyJourneys.entry: New Story and Existing Story; existing records plus local drafts; no sample records
storyJourneys.dismiss: Outside click, Escape, focus exit; keyboard arrows and click/touch supported
storyJourneys.theme: Existing surface, text, control, border tokens
storyJourneys.persistence: Workflow ID and intent fields saved with browser story setup; existing storage saves title/summary
storyJourneys.progress: Per-story browser-local last stage, script checkpoint, model settings and references; no completion inferred from navigation
storyJourneys.handoff: Exact storyboard narration seeds a new audio draft only; saved edits are preserved. Video carries story references and recordings only when unambiguous.
storyJourneys.review: Story-filtered audio/video assets with existing approve, download and trash controls; audio script export; completed output required for guided Review
storyJourneys.continuation: Next chapter/lesson/episode copies workflow and voice defaults, clears content, preserves prior story
storyJourneys.sourceMedia: Localization, repurposing and ambient journeys select source assets from actual libraries
storyJourneys.directEntry: Go to Studio bypasses guided entry
storyJourneys.backendLimits: No scheduler or new renderer added. YouTube needs an enabled configured backend. GPU jobs not tested by UI fixtures.
storyJourneys.entryConnections: Connection control panel remains clickable and keyboard-accessible on story selection; other header controls remain visible and inert until entering Studio.

googleSignIn.entry: Google-rendered Sign in with Google button on welcome screen only. Account and Billing does not show sign-in or its loading/error messages. Existing signed-in Log off remains. No intermediate Studio popup; Google account selection only.
googleSignIn.audience: Any Google account, no domain filter
googleSignIn.verification: Server-verified Google token with one-time nonce, audience, issuer and expiry checks; identity keyed by sub
googleSignIn.authorization: Identity session cannot access shared workspace API or start GPUs
googleSignIn.session: Opaque session token in sessionStorage; same-tab refresh restores only after server /me verification; expires within one hour. Log off revokes token and clears it and shared workspace key.
googleSignIn.dismiss: No intermediate Studio dialog. Google controls account-selection dismissal.
googleSignIn.appearance: Welcome Tell Your Story and native Google sign-in buttons have equal visible dimensions of 190px by 40px, with 16px between them. The native Google iframe transparent gutters are clipped to the button outline. Google SDK supplies unchanged logo, Google font and generic Sign in with Google text; width below 200px suppresses personalization. User menu is compact, minimum width 110px.
googleSignIn.signedInIdentity: Verified user name at far right after Education and Learning; visible dropdown arrow. Menu order: Credit and Usage, Billing, Log Off. Ribbon menu triggers share 36px height, 12px font, 10px horizontal padding and content-fit widths; user name capped at 220px; user dropdown items equal width and 40px height. Existing credit and billing actions reused. A decorative circular person icon appears immediately left of the name. The inner head and shoulders use the active theme accent; the outer ring uses theme text color. No separate keyboard stop.
googleSignIn.welcomeSignedIn: Signed in as <user name> replaces Google login after Studio verifies identity, including a restored session; Google browser session alone does not count as Studio login.

accountFlyouts.placement: Credit and Usage and Billing open to the left of the signed-in user dropdown; keep the parent dropdown open. Both also open left from the existing Account entries.
accountFlyouts.interaction: Hover or click a row; ArrowLeft opens and focuses the panel. Escape or ArrowRight closes only the panel and returns focus. Pointer/focus exit and parent dismissal close the panel. Only one account panel is shown at a time.
accountFlyouts.content: Reuse existing credit figures, Purchase Additional Credits flow, cost figures and Refresh costs action. No balance or permissions are inferred from sign-in.
accountFlyouts.appearance: Existing theme surface/text/border colors; circular person icon uses theme accent fill and theme text ring. Existing ribbon dimensions retained. Panels reveal from right to left with reduced-motion support.

googleSignIn.accountMenuVisibility: The separate Account and Billing ribbon dropdown is hidden, including from keyboard and accessibility navigation. Credit and Usage, Billing and Log Off remain in the signed-in user menu. The hidden legacy mount remains for compatibility with existing modules.
googleSignIn.signedOutIdentity: Rightmost header position shows the same theme-colored circular person icon with Not Logged in. Informational only, no account actions. Replaced by verified user dropdown on sign-in. Shares the compact header height (36px), 12px font and 10px horizontal padding; content-fit width.

publishingPlatforms.appearance: Six inline logo tabs; wrap on narrow screens. Background, border, text and selected accent resolve active --ecco-theme-* tokens directly, with Default fallbacks. Logos remain 18px.
publishingPlatforms.interaction: Same-window tab panels. Click, Left/Right arrows, Home/End; roving tab stop, aria-selected and linked tabpanel. Switching retains YouTube edits.
publishingPlatforms.availability: YouTube connection and confirmed uploads use the authenticated CPU storage service. Other platform connection rows and upload actions remain unavailable until their backend integration exists.
publishingPlatforms.source: Simple Icons SVG brand marks, bundled inline in publishing-platforms.js; attribution in assets/publishing/README.md.
publishingPlatforms.entry: Publish journey step opens tabs directly; no intermediate review text or Open publishing action.
publishingPlatforms.submit: One Publish button above tabs; disabled with visible explanation when no channel, destination choice or approved video is available, or selected platform is unsupported. Existing form validation and explicit upload confirmation remain required.
publishingPlatforms.youtubeAuthorization: Connections → YouTube → Connect opens Google synchronously from the user click after workspace and OAuth configuration are ready. Pending requests disable duplicate attempts. Backend-verified status updates the control panel and publishing destination selector without replacing drafts, platform selection or focus. Backend authorization, PKCE and token encryption are unchanged.
publishingPlatforms.youtubeSetup: Connections control panel owns the YouTube Connect/Connected and Disconnect controls. Connect remains enabled unless a request is in flight, and opens Set up YouTube before storage authentication when needed. The JSON file picker stays accessible; installation requires authenticated CPU setup availability. A separate Connect storage action opens a nested storage dialog and preserves the current page and selected file. Storage and Google secrets are never interchangeable. Closing a child preserves Connections and restores focus. Existing configuration discovered after storage login offers explicit Google authorization instead of replacement. No secrets are rendered or cached; bounded JSON goes only to the existing authenticated CPU endpoint.
publishingPlatforms.selection: The Publish navigation step remains active on the publishing page, using the existing theme-colored inset left highlight. Selected platform tabs use the same 3px inset left accent, replacing the bottom underline; no full accent border. Default yellow, active theme accent otherwise.
publishingPlatforms.forms: All six platforms retain editable video/title/description/visibility/audience and confirmation forms. Connection cards, Connect buttons and connection shortcuts are removed from Publishing. YouTube has a required destination dropdown populated only from authorized CPU channel metadata. Other platforms remain unavailable until backend integration exists.
publishingPlatforms.youtubeChannels: One verified YouTube channel per private workspace. Publishing shows its channel name, handle and ID. A changed destination clears confirmation; uploads verify ownership before queueing and again at worker start. Connections owns authorization and Disconnect.
publishingPlatforms.youtubeSchedule: Schedule in the existing Visibility dropdown reveals a registered date-time input using existing form styles. Browser-local time converts to UTC; backend requires a future timezone-qualified time and private upload. Other-platform forms do not expose scheduling. Completed uploads link to YouTube.
publishingPlatforms.connectionPlacementApproval: 2026-10-23: user requested the compact publishing control-panel icon and connected-platform dropdown, Connections-only management, spacing above Disconnect, multiple playlists (correcting the earlier channel request), and library-opening options inside the production-video chooser on every platform.
publishingPlatforms.controlPanel: 18px platform icon in existing 28px control slot, theme connected/disconnected colors. Click opens Connections, never uploads. When more than one authorized destination exists, adjacent dropdown lists each platform icon/channel/Connected. Unavailable or disconnected platforms are excluded. Arrow keys, Home/End, Escape, outside click and focus exit supported; Escape returns focus to trigger. No stored browser metadata is treated as authorization.
publishingPlatforms.connectionSpacing: User requested space above Disconnect in Connections; use 12px margin, matching the existing channel-label spacing.
publishingPlatforms.playlists: YouTube-only optional playlist dropdown lists every owned playlist, following API pagination. Create playlist dialog uses existing form/secondary/close styles, maximum width 540px and viewport margin 32px. Title, description, visibility (private default) and explicit confirmation; close returns focus. Create and refresh buttons use an 8px wrapping row. Loading/errors are announced; stale responses cannot change another channel. Creation and adding uploads require opt-in Enable playlists in Connections; existing upload grants remain valid. Failed playlist insertion retains the uploaded video and shows a warning, preventing a duplicate upload.
publishingPlatforms.libraryOptions: Each platform production-video chooser opens the existing Video or Audio Library in selection mode. Checkbox on every available item; Select all, Clear selection, Add selected (N), Cancel. Selections span stories, retain previews and survive library refresh/filter changes. Add selected returns to the originating platform with its draft and selected items; Cancel restores the original selection. Uploaded videos cannot be selected. Items have editable publishing titles and individual Remove buttons; shared description, visibility, audience and optional playlist apply to every selected video. Changing selection or titles clears explicit upload consent. Audio can be selected but YouTube publication explains that it requires video and remains disabled. No automatic conversion or GPU work.
publishingPlatforms.batchPublishing: Explicitly confirmed YouTube selection queues the existing authenticated single-video API once per approved video, with individual titles. Prevent concurrent submissions and re-submission of accepted or uncertain requests. Stop on a failed request, retain per-item status and direct the owner to Activity. Other platforms keep selections but uploads remain unavailable.
publishingPlatforms.pickerAppearance: Existing library cards/previews and form/button styles. Checkbox labels use 12px padding; selected-item rows wrap with 8px gap and 12px bottom margin; title labels flex with 180px minimum width. Selection controls remain keyboard accessible; empty state disables Add selected and focuses Cancel.
publishingPlatforms.publishingFeedback: User requested visible ongoing publishing and traceable Activity/Debugging/Errors. Publish shows a 16px circular theme-colored spinner, Publishing… and aria-busy during confirmed submission/queued/running work. A persistent status panel shows the last five attempts with real worker progress, timestamp, job/request ID, actual visibility and a YouTube link only after the server reports an uploaded video ID. Failures and uncertain outcomes are explicit; no synthetic progress or automatic upload retries. Completed uploads loaded from workspace records are recovered into history; reserved uploads without a known job remain unknown.
publishingPlatforms.publishingDiagnostics: Keep up to 50 credential-free attempts in this browser before calling youtube/publish, retaining returned server job IDs across navigation/reload. Activity lists all retained attempts even if submission failed before job creation. Debugging includes video/asset/channel IDs, status, progress, visibility, playlist and returned YouTube video ID; Errors records rejected/failed/unknown outcomes with redaction. Successful uploads do not create errors. Polling updates status without replacing draft fields or focus. Backend upload records remain authoritative; browser history is supplementary.

educationDiscord.label: Discord
educationDiscord.placement: Header, immediately right of Connections Control Panel, in a separate compact Community and source code panel with GitHub. Removed from Education and Learning. Trash stays in its original sidebar position.
educationDiscord.appearance: Same surface, border, radius and inset shadow as connection control panel; active theme tokens and glass surfaces. Matching existing 32px utility buttons and 16px icons.
educationDiscord.action: Opens existing theme-aware Discord dialog showing Not connected; shared close x and Escape; focus returns to Discord. No server configured.

sidebarGitHub.placement: Right of Discord in header Community and source code panel, beside Connections. Trash stays in sidebar.
sidebarGitHub.action: Open https://github.com/ecco-ai-labs/ecco-studio in new tab with noopener noreferrer. Accessible label announces new tab.
sidebarGitHub.appearance: Same 32px button area, 16px icon, theme-aware hover/focus and glass surface as the Discord panel.

audioScriptStudio.approval: User requested character counts and optional names with later per-character voice selection, plus a real AI script popup accepting a topic or uploaded paper and single-voice/multi-turn scripts. User requested a guided Audio journey with source-only extraction, questions, suggested reusable character profiles, editable turns and Apply to main fields.

characters.location: Characters section after References and before Spoken script
characters.count: 1–20 active characters, matching the existing 20-segment audio request limit
characters.defaults: News: 1 newsreader. Podcast, Interview and Casual Conversation: Host + Guest. Other genres: 1 narrator. Genre presets apply only before user cast customization or script content.
characters.identity: Stable character IDs, independent from voice IDs. Reducing the count keeps inactive names and settings for later reuse.
characters.voices: Additional Controls uses named character tabs, model-supported voices, language, emotion, dialect guidance and explicit voice preview.

scriptPopup.entry: Generate with AI on any Audio story setup or in Audio Studio Spoken script
scriptPopup.presentation: Native modal dialog appended to body, using generation-dialog styling, shared upper-right close button and focus return
fields: audience, genre, model-supported language, tone, purpose and source-specific questions
AI-proposed cast count, names, roles, gender, age group and personality/speaking style
saved character sets for reuse across chapters
turn count, optional spoken opening and pause
scriptPopup.uploads: Read locally, at most 20 MB and 20,000 source characters; disclose truncation. Selection replaces the source before any AI call. Read Source sends only that scope through the existing authenticated service. Never send the rest of an uploaded document, unrelated stories or chapters.
scriptPopup.review: Show editable speaker-assigned turns. Apply updates spoken script; generation never auto-starts speech. Cancel, stale state and invalid plans preserve the current script.
scriptPopup.news: Without selected scenes or source text, request current cited news through existing research service before writing narration; display cited sources in review.

audioScriptStudio.generation: Resolve character IDs to their latest voice/language/emotion when submitting existing audio/generate payload. Apply existing global speed, pitch and pause. Keep speech text separate from instructions.
audioScriptStudio.limits: Existing 4,000 spoken characters, 500 characters per speech segment and 20 speech segments remain enforced before Apply and Generate.
audioScriptStudio.workflowStatus: Scheduling requires the authenticated CPU workspace audio-workflow runner; UI publication alone does not activate schedules.

guidedJourney.apply: Main page and audio draft change only on Apply. Cancel, stale source/story state and invalid plans preserve existing fields. Save and Continue with Script saves edited narration and stable character-to-turn mappings.
guidedJourney.suggestions: Adult paper podcast: normally Host + Guest. Storybook: source-specific narrator and speaking cast. News: normally one newsreader. User edits count and all properties.
guidedJourney.persistence: Explicit Save Characters stores named character sets in this browser, with stable IDs and profile properties, for reuse across chapters. Disclose browser-local storage in UI.
guidedJourney.handoff: Title, genre, audience, language, tone, narration, cast directions, source and structured script populate the main form. Save preserves manual transcript edits and seeds audio voices and turns.
guidedJourney.appearance: Existing generation-dialog, field groups, theme tokens and upper-right close control. Four text steps with current-step accent, keyboard focus and Escape dismissal.
guidedJourney.interfaceLanguage: English for menus, clarification questions, source reviews, cast explanations and character-property descriptions, independently of the selected script language. Spoken content retains the selected language and native script; preserve source quotations and character proper names. All AI enhancement requests explicitly keep user-facing questions and notes in English.
guidedJourney.progress: Use the existing generation-spinner (16px, currentColor, existing reduced-motion behavior) in the primary action with Generating Script…, disabled duplicate submission and aria-busy. Preserve the current step and character edits while waiting. AI follow-up questions appear in Script Clarifications on the current Characters step, preserving earlier answers. Only a valid script advances to review; failures stop the spinner and allow retry in place.

languageStyle.placement: Questions before Generate Script, plus the main Audio setup. Custom shows a required free-text direction.
languageStyle.behavior: All UI labels stay English. The choice guides vocabulary and sentence complexity in the selected spoken language. Everyday Hindi requests common spoken words and short natural sentences, avoiding highly Sanskritized Hindi, difficult literary Urdu and literal translation. The selected style and custom instructions survive Apply, save, reopen and next-chapter handoff.

audioWorkflowScheduling.approval: User requested automatic generation of news, podcasts and storybooks for the weekend goal.
audioWorkflowScheduling.activation: Authenticated workspace capability required. Saving pauses the schedule; Enable Schedule is explicit. Run Now does not disable an existing schedule.
audioWorkflowScheduling.persistence: Definitions and run history belong to the existing CPU workspace service. Browser drafts are not running schedules.
audioWorkflowScheduling.recovery: Stable run and audio job IDs prevent duplicate audio after restart. Interrupted AI calls pause without paid automatic retry.
audioWorkflowScheduling.availability: Selected compute only; no fallback or provisioning. Controls stay unavailable until storage connects and the updated runner is advertised.
audioWorkflowScheduling.deletion: Pause persisted audio schedules successfully before moving them to this browser Trash.
audioWorkflowScheduling.scope: Automatic audio generation and saving; publishing is separate. Existing layout, themes and model controls are reused.

eccoDesk.appearance: Preserves the user-approved Desk design: navy sidebar, yellow primary action, light ticket surfaces. Studio retains its selected theme and existing header dimensions. Desk CSS is scoped in a shadow root so it never restyles Studio. Embedded support hides the standalone sidebar, topbar and footer. Its sign-in panel and page heading inherit Studio theme text, surface, border and accent; ticket surfaces retain the approved light Desk style. The headset reuses community-panel theme text, accent hover/focus and focus outline, with transparent button background; SVG strokes stay visible and do not shrink.
eccoDesk.layout: Support uses a headset with microphone beside Discord/GitHub, inside the existing 32px asset-icon button with a 16px glyph. Support renders in the main page with Back to Studio. No team-workspace link appears on the customer surface. Desk retains its metric cards, scrollable table, right detail drawer and centered dialogs.
eccoDesk.content: Ecco Desk branding; internal tasks, customer support, personal assignments, explicit team access, activity history. Customer support shows only the requester’s support tickets.
eccoDesk.states: Loading, signed out, empty, error, filtered empty, populated, busy, open dialog/drawer. Errors use role=alert and success uses role=status; network requests time out. Refresh rechecks server permissions.
eccoDesk.interaction: Header Support opens inside Studio without needing storage/GPU access. Existing Google sign-in is reused on welcome with a return intent. Esc dismisses the current Desk dialog/drawer; focus is trapped and returned, including within Shadow DOM. Tab order follows the visible content. No nested Desk dialogs.
eccoDesk.accessibility: Support icon has an accessible name. Forms have labels, constraints and inline errors. Dialog/drawer have named dialog roles and aria-modal. Icon-only actions are named; decorative SVG icons are hidden. Reduced motion supported.
eccoDesk.authorization: Server verifies existing opaque Google session. Identity is keyed by Google sub. Customers cannot see other tickets, internal notes, staff directory or staff audit data. Roles never come from email/domain. First administrator explicitly activates using existing workspace access plus verified identity; later grants refer to an existing verified account. No email invitations are sent. Studio uses /api/desk/support: every request uses requester permissions even for staff/admin identities; lists, details, replies and history are limited to the authenticated Google subject. The endpoint never returns members, internal notes, team activity or setup controls, and rejects team operations. Separately authorized team operations remain on /api/desk. Account changes clear cached tickets and discard responses for the previous identity.
eccoDesk.storage: Existing CPU storage API and SQLite on persistent Ecco volume. Dedicated desk_* tables are excluded from legacy workspace records. No tickets, tokens or access keys are stored in GitHub Pages/source. Separate ChatGPT login is not used.
eccoDesk.build: Run npm ci && npm run build in desk/. Checked-in desk-app.mjs is the generated browser bundle; authored TSX/CSS are included in the inventory.
